criteria.text:
A `PG_SSL_CA` value containing literal `
` (two-char) escape sequences, e.g. `"-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMII...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n"` (as a JS string, i.e. the actual bytes are backslash-n, not newline), normalizes to real newlines in the string `poolConfig(...).ssl.ca` includes — checked by splitting on real `
` and asserting more than one line, or by asserting the normalized string equals the same PEM built with real `
` characters.

The same holds for literal `
` (four-char) sequences: normalizes to a real `
` at each occurrence, not a real `` followed by a literal `
`.

A `PG_SSL_CA` value that already contains real embedded newlines and no literal backslash-escape sequences is passed through byte-identical (existing test at `test/db.test.ts` ~line 62–71 keeps passing unmodified).
A `PG_SSL_CA` value that, after normalization, does not contain `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` throws synchronously with a message matching `/PG_SSL_CA/`, for a non-local host only.

For a local host (`localhost` or `127.0.0.1`), `poolConfig(...).ssl` is `undefined` regardless of `PG_SSL_CA`'s content or presence, including a non-PEM value that would throw on a non-local host — normalization and the PEM check never run.
`poolConfig(...).ssl.ca` remains a single array with exactly `tls.rootCertificates.length + 1` entries after normalization (normalization must not split one certificate into multiple array entries).
`src/push.ts` requires no code change: it still builds its pool with `poolConfig(url)` alone (existing regex test in `test/db.test.ts` keeps passing), so it inherits normalization automatically.
The comment directly above `poolConfig` still matches `test/db.test.ts`'s existing regex check (mentions `PG_SSL_CA`, mentions `verif`, never says "without chain verification").

`docsText` (the concatenation `test/docs.ts` exposes) states that either a literal-escaped or a real-newline `PG_SSL_CA` value is now accepted — a new criterion, not covered by any existing test: assert `docsText` matches a pattern naming both forms, e.g. `/PG_SSL_CA[\s\S]{0,400}(literal|escaped)[\s\S]{0,400}newline/i` or equivalent, phrased against the fact (both forms accepted), not against exact wording.

`docsText` no longer instructs the reader to run `printf '%b'` on `PG_SSL_CA` as a required step (the old workaround is gone because it's no longer necessary) — assert `docsText` does not match `/printf '%b'/`.

The two existing `docsText` assertions (`PG_SSL_CA`/`CA certificate`/`PEM`/fail-closed language; `PG_SSL_CA` co-occurring with `Vercel` and with `DATABASE_URL`/`POSTGRES_URL`) keep passing unmodified.
`test/docs-drift.test.ts`'s existing checks are unrelated to this change (no collector, no source) and need no new criterion here — confirmed, not extended.
